verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. `SlowStressSupport.stress m F (r,η)` unfolds to -(∫_0^r F(x,η)dx)/r^m for r > 0, which is the paper's formula once F is the weighted residual and m is 2 or 1: the factors s² and s sit inside F rather than in the integrand, because `thetaDensity` is the literal R²-weighted angular residual and `zDensity` the literal R-weighted axial residual (their own docstrings, and the order-zero computation `leading_thetaDensity`/`leading_zDensity`, ZerothStressIdentity.lean:140,153). The exponent 3 in the body of `thetaDensity` (R³/C, against R in `zDensity`) is not a mismatch with the paper's s²: the swirl is encoded with its own factor R/C, `swirlRadius C f w = (w.1/C)·f(radiusPoint w)` (SlowResidualMatching.lean:362), where the axial component uses the plain `toRadius` (line 360), and the leading φ-profile is C·P.f (the φ-component of `leadingProfiles` is reduced to `C * P.f q` at ZerothStressIdentity.lean:206); so R²·R_θ = (R³/C)·angularCoefficient while R·R_z = R·axialCoefficient. The pairing is checked at order zero in the file: `weightedTheta_eq` (ZerothStressIdentity.lean:125) gives weightedTheta = R²·LeadingStress.theta and `weightedAxial_eq` (:132) gives weightedAxial = R·LeadingStress.axial, and the R-derivatives of those weighted quantities (`weightedTheta_hasDerivAt`, :91, and `weightedAxial_hasDerivAt`, :108) are exactly minus the right-hand sides of `leading_thetaDensity` (:140) and `leading_zDensity` (:153). Differences, all conventional: (i) the Lean definition is extended by the value 0 for r ≤ 0, which the paper does not mention — the paper instead says "Regularity at the axis fixes their integration constants", and that lower endpoint 0 is what the Lean primitive uses; (ii) `thetaDensity` carries the swirl normalisation 1/C, matching `leadingProfiles.phi = C * P.f`, so the quotient is again the unnormalised stress — at order zero `raw_stresses_eq` (ZerothStressIdentity.lean:281) proves this primitive-defined stress equals the explicitly constructed `LeadingStress.theta`/`LeadingStress.axial`, so the identity itself and not only the notation is checked; (iii) in the slow hierarchy the density used is the conservative form `angularDensity`/`axialDensity`, equal to the literal weighted residual `angularWeighted` under the divergence-free hypothesis (`angularWeighted_eq_density`, SlowStressSupport.lean:458). The differentiated form of the same relation, d/dr(r² T) = -(r² R_θ), appears as the third conjunct of `angular_stress_support` (SlowStressSupport.lean:982), under the order restriction 2 ≤ n.
